patterns: The outage/cyber story stayed on top: 39 hits (~2.44M views) at a 3.0% like rate, up from 0.6% yesterday. Laura Ingraham 'screamed' over CISA's 22 months with no confirmed director ~560k (3.4%), Duffy's 2002 L3Harris air traffic contract ~251k (4.4%), Bongino's 'AI gave hackers a nail gun' ~207k, rawsalerts mocking 'no evidence of a targeted cyberattack' ~179k, Starlink pitch ~111k (4.4%). Accountability and fixes earned likes; pure alarm (survival gear sales +2000% ~165k, 1.0%) did not
The top post was a one-liner with no news hook: Gunther's 'if war ever reaches American soil, citizens are NOT required to follow military rules of engagement' ~623k at 2.5%

Short opinion lines owned the like rates again: 'Texas is not a blue state. We need an audit of every vote' ~62k at 12.0%, Burchett-for-Senate ask ~34k at 12.5%, 'Jesus Christ already lives in the hearts and homes' ~54k at 12.5%, 'John Thune f*cked us all' ~80k at 10.4%, Iran hitman sentenced 27.5 years ~65k at 10.3%

Outage-to-election-security crossover worked: 16 vote/audit/voting-machine hits (~695k) at 6.8%, e.g. 'Everything is hackable... except electronic voting machines' ~33k at 9.5% and 'If they can hack the banks, they can hack our elections' ~44k at 9.1%
'Hey @grok' questions cooled off: only 3 hits (~162k) at 0.4%, led by 'play intelligence analyst, connect the dots on FAA, Apple, Microsoft and railroad' ~118k

Other lines: Trump's Asia/China trip (Kim meeting, three-way Xi-Putin arms talks) 17 hits ~438k at 3.2%; Iran (Qeshm Island strike, hitman sentence) 8 hits ~339k at 5.3%; Ilhan Omar investigation 3 hits ~152k; Peltola flips Alaska ~90k. rawsalerts was back with 5 originals (~823k), led by the D.C. shooter probation story ~362k; alx had 25, led by the Musk/Trump reinstatement anniversary ~326k
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, ~50 posts) was quiet again, with nothing past ~24k. The biggest AI story crossing into politics was Google's warning that 'the era of autonomous attacks has arrived', AI turning security patches into working exploits with no human involved (@TMLwire ~24k; many small copies, plus an FBI flash advisory on the ARTEX AI hacking tool ~1.3k). Business news was Sam Altman praising Jensen Huang after his exit from Nvidia (@the_hindu ~9.6k, @CNBCTV18News ~6.3k), Microsoft unveiling 6 AI models at Ignite (~6.6k), Nvidia's $115.8B quarter and Anthropic setting an IPO range of $70-78 (a few thousand views each). Open lane: plain-English 'what autonomous AI attacks mean for you' explainers. Gunther's Watters/Google post did ~40k at 1.4% and Bongino's AI-hackers clip ~207k, but no outsider has done a calm, practical version.
narrative_synthesis: A Tuesday-to-Wednesday window: 181 hits from 186 originals, ~8.31M views. The outage wave turned from panic into accountability. CISA's 22 months without a director, a 2002 air traffic contract, and the DNI saying the outages were separate maintenance problems, not an attack. Those posts got real likes (3-4%), unlike yesterday's doom posts (0.6%). The best like rates still went to short opinion lines (12%+) and to tying outages to paper-ballot election security (6.8%). @grok questions faded. Takeaway: on day 3 of a crisis, post who's responsible and what to do. People have already seen the alarm.
